title: OpenAI's Aura check can refuse a site even when robots.txt allows it

drafts.text: A Search Engine Journal report says ChatGPT's browsing can refuse a site under a safety check called Aura, even when robots.txt allows access. One publisher's account, 29 Oct 2026. Our scanner reads robots.txt, not this check.
thread: The article says a flagged site is refused even when settings and robots.txt allow it. The block is cached for 24 hours, and it reports no public appeal process.

Test before you assume a robots.txt problem: load your key URLs in ChatGPT live fetch and on a control site. If only yours fail and your server logs show no request, the block is upstream of your rules.
Keep the evidence: timestamped screenshots, the exact error text, and crawler logs for GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User.
Method: one publisher, as reported by SEJ on 29 Oct 2026. We have not tested Aura on any site. Confidence: low.

drafts.text:
Search Engine Journal reported today that ChatGPT's browsing can refuse a site under a safety check called Aura, even when robots.txt allows the crawler. The article reports blocks cached for 24 hours and no public appeal process.

This changes how I read a readiness scan. Our scanner reads robots.txt, llms.txt and the homepage. A block made outside those files would not show up in a scan, so a clean scan does not prove that assistants can reach a page.

What I would check first: load your key URLs through ChatGPT's live fetch and through a control site, then compare your server logs. The article says a block leaves no request in your logs at the moment of the failed attempt.

Method note: one publisher's account, reported by Search Engine Journal on 29 Oct 2026. I have not tested this on any site. Confidence: low.
